2.    The Investigating Officer, while opposing the case of the
applicant for being released on bail before the trial court, pleaded
that the applicant has many small and big pan kiosks and,
therefore, assumed that he must have more contraband articles
with him and this is cited as a reason for seeking his custodial
interrogation. On the basis of the said say of the Investigating
Officer, the Sessions Judge, Kalyan, in the order dated
18/01/2022 branded him as stockist, who had provided the
contraband articles. When learned A.P.P. was asked to provide
the material to that aspect, he was unable to lay his hands upon
any such material.
3.    The case of the prosecution is to the effect that, on an
information received on 29/10/2021 to the effect that certain
prohibited substance like tobacco, gutka, pan masala are stored
in a godown located behind Najami General Stores, Mahatma
Phule Chowk, Ulhasnagar, a raid was conducted and, on search,
the prohibited substances like tobacco, scented betel nuts and
allied products were found in huge quantity. This led to the
arrest of one Salim Bhagwan, who owed the said godown and
this led the Investigating Officer to the present applicant.
4.    The sketchy connection projected by the main accused in
respect of the present applicant on the ground that the applicant
is telephonically in touch with the main accused, has led to his

indictment in the present FIR.
5.     As per the learned counsel for the applicant, the applicant
is a young man of 29 years and an IT professional and he has no
connection with the C.R., in which he is arraigned as an accused.
Learned counsel submits that the applicant is ready to render all
co-operation with the Investigating Officer.          Upon such
assurance being given, the applicant needs to be protected.
Hence, the following order:

texts.facts_text: On 29/10/2021, an information was received that certain prohibited substances like tobacco, gutka, pan masala were stored in a godown behind Najami General Stores, Mahatma Phule Chowk, Ulhasnagar. A raid was conducted, and prohibited substances were found in large quantities, leading to the arrest of Salim Bhagwan, who owned the godown. This led the Investigating Officer to the present applicant, Sushant Sunil Singh, based on a sketchy connection that he was telephonically in touch with the main accused.
texts.arguments_petitioner: The applicant, Sushant Sunil Singh, is a young IT professional with no connection to the case. He is willing to cooperate with the Investigating Officer and needs protection.
texts.arguments_respondent: The Investigating Officer opposed the applicant's release on bail, citing that the applicant has many pan kiosks and might possess contraband articles, necessitating custodial interrogation. However, the Sessions Judge, Kalyan, branded him as a stockist without providing material evidence.

(b) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with facts of case and shall not tamper with prosecution evidence. (c) The applicant shall report to the Ulhasnagar Police Station, Dist. Thane on 7/03/2022, 09/03/2022 and 11/03/2022 between 10.00 a.m. and 2.30 p.m. and co-operate with the investigation.

key_facts_bullets: Information received on 29/10/2021 about prohibited substances stored in a godown behind Najami General Stores.
Raid conducted, resulting in the arrest of Salim Bhagwan.
Investigating Officer linked Sushant Sunil Singh to the case based on a telephonic connection.
issues_bullets: Whether the applicant should be granted anticipatory bail.
Assessing the credibility of the Investigating Officer's claims regarding the applicant's involvement.
